title: Scorn Not the Slightest Word or Deed
description: Scorn Not the Slightest Word or Deed in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 307, “Effort”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Scorn not the slight-est word or deed, Nor deem it void of power; There's fruit in each wind waft-ed seed, That waits its na-tal hour.

lines: Scorn not the slightest word or deed,
Nor deem it void of power;
There's fruit in each wind-wafted seed,
A whispered word may touch the heart,
And call it back to life;
A look of love bid sin depart,
No act falls fruitless; none can tell
How vast its power may be,
Work on, despair not; bring thy mite,
Nor care how small it be;
God is with all that serve the right,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1848.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
